fnd_01K5RTGH.counterfactual: one grouped-totals call per run · 1,900 tok
method: Measured
Every aws_billing__get_cost_and_usage call returned a full month of daily line items: 41,200 tokens on average, unpaged.
Re-read
The result stays in the window, so each of the 6 to 9 later turns on the run paid input price on it again.
Never used
The frames show the model summing the line items to service totals on 86 of 88 runs. The rows themselves were never cited.
Counterfactual
Ask for service totals grouped by month (1,900 tokens) and page rows only when a turn drills into one service. Difference × turns × the input price on each call.

who.note: Dana ported the report from a notebook that pulled everything and summed in pandas. The agent inherited the query shape and does the sum in the context window.

fnd_01K5RTEG.signal: identical command digests inside a turn window
fnd_01K5RTEG.counterfactual: one execution per identical command until a write
method: Measured
2,741 of 8,841 claude_code__Bash calls repeated a command whose input digest matched a call earlier in the same run, with no write in between.
Same answer
On 2,690 of 2,741 repeats the result digest matched the earlier result. The other 51 followed a clock or a network read.
Paid twice
Each repeat costs the call, the 4.1k-token result body re-entering the window, and the turn spent deciding to re-run.
Counterfactual
Serve the cached result inside the turn window; invalidate on any write. Remove the repeat calls and the tokens they added to every later turn.

who.note: The harness has no result cache; the model re-runs git status and ls to reassure itself. Marcus never saw it because each call is cheap on its own.

fnd_01K5RTJI.baseline: 2 changes to the list this month
fnd_01K5RTJI.counterfactual: one fetch per change, served from a workspace cache
method: Measured
slack__list_channels was called once on 341 of 341 runs that later posted to Slack, always as the first tool call.
Same answer
The result digest was identical on 339 of 341 calls. The list changed on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-09.
Paid every run
3,400 tokens of channel metadata entered 341 contexts and stayed there for every later turn.
Counterfactual
Two fetches, served from a workspace-scoped cache with a 24-hour TTL. Everything else is saved.

who.note: The agent's brief says to resolve the channel by name before posting. Resolving means listing, and nothing told it the list was stable.

fnd_01K5RT4B.trend: one-off · recurs on every mid-day publish
method: Measured
Between 2026-09-04 11:20 UTC and 2026-09-06 the cache-read share on core-platform fell from 88% to 61%.
Cause pinned
The drop starts at the frame where ctx.release.notes-format was published. The system-context digest changed inside 212 live conversations.
Baseline
The seven days before the publish sat at 88% ± 2; the seven after the caches warmed sat at 87%.
Counterfactual
Re-price the 1,908 model calls in the window at the baseline cache share. The difference is the saving.

fnd_01K5RT6C.signal: identical tool input digests within a run
fnd_01K5RT6C.counterfactual: one github__get_file_contents@2 of CHANGELOG.md per run
method: Measured
github__get_file_contents@2 was called with an identical input digest an average of 3.2 times per run on a-intel.core.release-manager.
Same answer
On 682 of 682 repeats the response digest matched the first read. Nothing changed between reads.
Paid twice
Each repeat costs the tool call, the 2,900-token response re-entering the window, and the turn the model spent deciding to re-read.
Counterfactual
One read per run. Remove the repeat calls and the tokens they added to every later turn.

who.note: The agent's brief says “confirm the changelog before each section”. It reads the whole file every time it confirms.

method: Measured
91% of a-intel.core.triage steps are classification-shaped: one label out of a fixed set, under 400 output tokens.
Escalation
When a light-tier call times out, the harness retries on the complex route. 14% of the agent's model calls landed on claude-opus-5 that way.
Same output
On 188 of 191 escalated calls the label matched what the light tier had already produced on the same input elsewhere.
Counterfactual
Re-price the escalated calls at the light tier. Medium confidence because 3 of 191 differed.

who.note: The agent's fallback route is the workspace default, which is the complex tier. Nobody chose it; nobody un-chose it.

fnd_01K5RTAE.signal: steps after the last kept side effect
fnd_01K5RTAE.counterfactual: stop two steps after the last kept effect
method: Measured
On 41 of 64 runs, six or more steps followed the last step whose side effect survived to the sealed run.
What they did
Those tail steps re-read the file just written, re-listed the directory, and asked the model whether it was done: 2.1 model calls per tail step.
Nothing kept
No tail step produced a side effect that the run kept. The diff of the kept files is empty before and after the tail.
Counterfactual
Cut each run two steps after its last kept effect. The tail's model calls are the saving.

who.note: The agent's loop has no stop rule; it ends when the model says it is done, and the model checks its work several times before saying so.

fnd_01K5RTCF.signal: cache_write_5m with no cache_read inside the TTL
fnd_01K5RTCF.counterfactual: no cache write on one-turn runs
method: Measured
On 28 one-turn runs under Priya's operator id, the only model call wrote a 5-minute cache prefix.
Never read
No later call read that prefix inside the TTL. The next run of the same agent started 40 minutes later on average.
Paid for nothing
A cache write costs 1.25× the input price. The write was the whole premium; nothing was returned.
Counterfactual
Price those 28 calls without the write premium.

who.note: Priya's invoice runs are scheduled one at a time, forty minutes apart. The agent's request builder marks the system block cacheable on every call regardless.
